newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Nagorno-Karabakh row threatens to upset summit.
newsitem.headline: Nagorno-Karabakh row threatens to upset summit.

text.p: Azerbaijan President Heydar Aliyev appealed on Monday for a swift agreement on a peace settlement over Nagorno-Karabakh but Armenia said the Azeri government was unable to guarantee the safety of the people in the enclave.
The dispute threatened to disrupt efforts to agree a final document at the two-day summit of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE).
Aliyev told more than 50 OSCE leaders that Armenia was intent on pursuing independence for Nagorno-Karabakh, an enclave with an ethnic Armenian majority surrounded by Azeri territory.

The president said his framework peace proposal called for recognition of Azerbaijan's territorial integrity, an assurance of a high degree of autonomy for Nagorno-Karabakh and security guarantees for all the enclave's population.
"It is regrettable that the Republic of Armenia refuses to accept such a formula...It refuses to accept the territorial integrity of the Azerbaijani republic," Aliyev told the summit.
"We cannot allow the creation on the territory of Azerbaijan of a second Armenian state," he said. "We do not want war. We want peace."

Azerbaijan wants its territorial integrity to be reaffirmed in the Lisbon summit final document, similar to a passage in a draft paper which expresses the OSCE's "utmost support for the sovereignty and territorial integrity" of Georgia.
But Armenia is opposed to any reference to Azerbaijan's territorial integrity.

Up to one million Azeris have lived in tent camps since ethnic Armenians drove Azeris out of the enclave in a six-year war triggered by Nagorno-Karabakh's independence declaration in 1988. Some 10,000 people were killed in the fighting.

Armenian President Levon Ter-Petrossian said it was because of several "pogroms" of ethnic Armenians by Azerbaijan since 1988 that he believed only self-determination of Nagorno-Karabakh would ensure the safety of its people.
"Despite any and all assurances that may be given, Azerbaijan is unable to guarantee the security of the population of Nagorno-Karabakh," Ter-Petrossian told the summit.
"That is why we consider that the only possible way to prevent further tragedy is to ensure the rights of the people of Nagorno-Karabakh to self-determination," he added.
But the Armenian president repeated a pledge to take part in talks to try to find a peaceful settlement and cooperate with the 11-nation Minsk Group, a mediation body set up by the OSCE.
A fragile ceasefire has existed since May 1994, but both sides have failed to agree a peace settlement. Talks in Helsinki mediated by the Minsk Group broke down last month.
The OSCE summit in Budapest in 1994 agreed to prepare a multinational peacekeeping force for Nagorno-Karabakh, but deployment cannot go ahead until both sides agree peace.

OSCE sources said the dispute could disrupt efforts to put together a final declaration at the Lisbon summit. Azerbaijan could hinder, or block, a final summit document if it fails to win affirmation of its territorial integrity.
